## 2. Overnight world read (verified outside the bus)
**Maritime veto layer — the reversal level broke. The falsifier ledgered since 2026-09-15 fired.**
- Brent Thursday PRELIMINARY close 104.08 (Yahoo plugin BZ=F, vol 54 — thin); Yahoo's own web table prints 104.16 (vol 20); convextrade prints 103.89 (-1.60%). Three sources, 27c spread, same direction: UNDER the 104.61 reversal level.
- Per the falsifier carried since the 09-15 signal ("veto upgrade reverses if Brent settles under $104.61"): REVERSAL TRIGGERED, pending final-settle confirmation. Caveat is not decorative — two straight cycles of Yahoo close revisions, and a vol-54 print is not a settle I would countersign without tomorrow's confirmation.
- NEW MATERIAL — second bypass channel: Saudi Arabia is offering additional crude cargoes to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar, Oman (HDFC Sky, Sep 17). Yanbu Red Sea loadings remain suspended; damage is to two East-West pumping stations; repair timeline still unclear (Reuters via HDFC). Market is pricing the bypass (escorted Hormuz flow + Sohar STS) over the outage.
- Revision ledger: Sep-16 Brent close revised UP 105.58 → 105.83 (Yahoo) — resolving exactly toward Newsquawk's 105.83 November-contract settle. Yesterday's contract-roll hypothesis is now supported, and the Sep-16 105.83 row carries volume 51,174 — identical to Sep-15. Feed copy artifact; flagged, not resolved.

**Rates channel — BoE held; the 5% 10Y close did not follow through; BoJ is today's event.**
- BoE HELD Bank Rate at 3.75% Thursday (RTTNews, 08:54 ET item), as priced (Robinhood market had hold at 99¢). No surprise.
- US data Thursday: initial jobless claims unexpectedly fell to the lowest since mid-July (RTTNews); housing starts unexpectedly soft. Labor side stays firm post-hike.
- 10Y UST prelim Thursday close 4.947% (^TNX) — back under 5% after Wednesday's 5.006 first-close-above. The break lasted one session. S&P 500 prelim 7,637.76 (+1.14%) — Wednesday's post-dots fade fully retraced.
- BoJ decision due Friday, announcement any time after 03:30 BST / 22:30 EDT (Tokyo lunch window). +25bp to 1.25% fully priced (Newsquawk preview; Reuters poll 66 of 68; robomacro briefing). August nationwide CPI lands 08:30 JST Friday, hours before the statement. Ueda presser 15:30 JST. Priced move — the reaction lives in the guidance. Quad witching in the US Friday: don't over-read Friday closes.

**Crypto — SOL reclaimed $100; both posture-reopening legs still unmet.**
- BTC PRELIMINARY Thursday close 76,420.92 (H 76,968.79 / L 75,951.20), +0.4% vs the revised 76,150.32. Revision: Sep-16 close 76,018.02 → 76,150.32.
- SOL PRELIMINARY Thursday close 101.49 (H 101.84 / L 98.46), +2.9% vs revised 98.64 — the $100 reclaim watch item TRIGGERED on the prelim print. Revision: Sep-16 close 98.34 → 98.64. One close is not a hold; the bar for posture review remains BTC through 78,900 with SOL holding $103.
- Data-path check: Binance route FAILED for both BTCUSDT and SOLUSDT this cycle ("EMPTY_DATA — all symbol queries failed") after yesterday's partial (BTC ok / SOL 451). Ledger: DEGRADED → DISCONNECTED. Yahoo path verified live this cycle (BZ=F, BTC-USD, SOL-USD, ^TNX, ^GSPC dailies pulled via agent-gw).

## 3. Interrogation notes
- No new thesis on the bus to interrogate. Idle directive — what orbital and nova left unfalsified, unchanged: Nova CONCUR/VETO on argus_002 (maritime→energy KILL), argus_003 (FBX-SCFI KILL + Branch 0), post-hoc on T-2026-09-11-001, and the campus-split + eval-table CONCUR/VETO requested in orbital_001 (Sep 10). Nine cycles on the oldest item. Alex: the L1 clock workflow paste remains the one human action owed.
- Process: the PRELIMINARY-close rule kept us honest again — Sep-16 closes revised on all three tracks (Brent/BTC/SOL), direction intact, magnitudes moved. Three consecutive revision cycles is now the standing Yahoo data-quality pattern. Today's Brent call is explicitly hostage to the final settle.
- Self-interrogation on the reversal call: the outage itself is NOT resolved — Yanbu suspended, two pumping stations damaged, timeline unclear. What reversed is the market's escalation pricing, not the physical disruption. If the bypass channels stumble (escort flow, Sohar STS uptake), the premium can rebuild fast. Reversal of the upgrade ≠ all-clear.

1. TICKET.json (`open_waiting_nova`) vs adjudicated outcome (expired flat by process). Seventh cycle unresolved.
2. Brent Sep-16: 105.58 (ledgered prelim) vs 105.83 (revised) — resolved toward Newsquawk; supports the contract-roll read.
3. Brent Sep-17: 104.08 (plugin, vol 54) vs 104.16 (Yahoo web, vol 20) vs 103.89 (convextrade) — thin-print spread; direction unambiguous, exact settle pending.
4. BTC Sep-16: 76,018.02 (ledgered) vs 76,150.32 (revised). SOL Sep-16: 98.34 (ledgered) vs 98.64 (revised).
5. Brent Sep-15 and Sep-16 rows carry identical volume 51,174 — Yahoo feed copy artifact.
6. Hormuz flow: Kpler 4 commodity transits Monday (Reuters) vs US-official 40/day average (Axios via ISW). Still unresolved; Sohar STS is now a third flow channel to track.
7. Strike dating: ISW Sep-10 vs Fortune/AP closure Friday Sep-11 vs a third table's Sep-14. Range carried.
8. fearGreed 69 'Greed' from the Sep-10 paper tape — UNSOURCED, eighth consecutive cycle. CITE failure stands.
9. 10Y: first close above 5% Wednesday (5.006) vs 4.947 Thursday — the regime break did not follow through.

## 5. Watch list (T+1)
- Brent: final Thursday settle confirmation. Under 104.61 confirms the veto-upgrade reversal; a revision back above (the revision pattern cuts both ways) reopens it. Friday's settle is the tiebreak.
- BoJ decision and Ueda presser Friday; August Japan CPI at 08:30 JST pre-statement. A hold against full pricing is the tail that moves USD/JPY and the long end.
- Quad witching Friday — volume/pinning noise; closes carry less information than usual.
- Sohar STS uptake by Asian refiners; Yanbu loading resumption; repair timeline on the two pumping stations.
- SOL: second consecutive close above $100 to upgrade the reclaim from print to hold. BTC: 78,900 remains the posture-review trigger.
- War-risk insurance quote — unsourced, seventh cycle (stale baseline: ~8x pre-war, early July).

The veto upgrade REVERSES pending final-settle confirmation; the physical disruption is unresolved, so this is premium deflation under re-routing, not an all-clear. Rates delivered no new shock: BoE held 3.75% as priced, the 10Y's first close above 5% failed to follow through (4.947% prelim), equities retraced the post-dots fade (+1.14% prelim), and a fully priced BoJ +25bp to 1.25% lands within hours with the reaction living in Ueda's guidance. Crypto stabilized further (BTC prelim 76,421; SOL prelim 101.49 — $100 reclaimed on one print) but the posture-reopening bar (BTC 78,900 with SOL holding $103) is unmet. Flat/cash remains the only process-grade posture.
